questions.q: What must an Outbound Message be tied to in order to fire?
questions.explain: An Outbound Message is configured together with a Workflow Rule, which must be activated for the message to fire when its criteria are met.

questions.q: What format does Outbound Messaging send its notification in, and what must the receiving endpoint send back to stop retries?
options: GraphQL; the endpoint must return a success boolean
CSV; the endpoint must return the record's Id
JSON; the endpoint must return HTTP 204
SOAP/XML; the endpoint must return a SOAP acknowledgment envelope containing <Ack>true</Ack> over HTTP 200
questions.explain: Outbound Messaging sends a SOAP/XML message and requires an <Ack>true</Ack> SOAP envelope with HTTP 200 as acknowledgment, or Salesforce retries for up to 24 hours.

questions.q: What format does the modern Flow HTTP Callout action support?
questions.explain: Flow HTTP Callouts support JSON request and response bodies only, unlike Outbound Messaging's SOAP/XML format.

questions.q: What does setting up a Flow HTTP Callout action generate, based on a sample request and response?
options: An External Service, an API spec, and an invocable action the Flow can call directly
A Workflow Rule and an Outbound Message
questions.explain: Salesforce parses the sample request/response into a schema and generates an External Service, API spec, and invocable action — all without hand-written integration code.

questions.q: What built-in behavior does Outbound Messaging have that a Flow HTTP Callout does not provide automatically?
options: Support for authentication via Named Credentials
Automatic retry for up to 24 hours if no acknowledgment is received
The ability to batch more than 100 notifications
questions.explain: Outbound Messaging automatically retries sending for up to 24 hours if it doesn't receive an acknowledgment; a Flow HTTP Callout has no equivalent built-in retry and must handle that logic itself if needed.
